FILING_DESTINATION.detail: Scored under amendment A1: ask first whether the repository establishes the answer. It does — packet-family-build-worklist.json records filingDestination as 'recorded' with entries 'clerk of the original court' and 'court in the original criminal case', and the ND memo's auto-close track names 'The court that entered the order of nonconviction'. The packet states exactly that, twice: the written request goes 'to the office of the court in the original criminal case', and the enforcement motion is filed 'in the original criminal case'. The destination is stated, not deferred to an authority.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: Scored under DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001, asking first whether the repository establishes the answer. It does not: packet-family-build-worklist.json records filingFee and feeWaiverTreatment both as 'not_recorded' for this family. I checked the near neighbours before accepting that, because a wrong borrowing here would be easy — the ND memo's nd-nonconviction-close-petition track does state 'none. N.D.C.C. § 12-60.1-05(4) and the official instructions both state there is no filing fee', but that is a DIFFERENT instrument on a different branch (the pre-2025 petition, which this receipt expressly separates and does not carry), and the auto-close track's own 'fees: none' belongs to the automatic parent where nothing is filed at all. Neither answers whether a motion to enforce in an existing criminal case carries a fee. The packet says precisely that and names a specific reachable authority: 'Whether a filing fee applies to the enforcement motion, and how the request or motion must be delivered. Neither is established by the committed records this packet is built from. The office of the court in the original criminal case is the authority that can answer both — ask before you send or file.' That is the determination's third met-branch, and the refusal is the honest one rather than a borrowed figure.

SERVICE.detail: Scored on the same footing. packet-family-build-worklist.json records serviceRecipients, serviceMethod, certificateOfService and notice all as 'not_recorded' for this family, and the auto-close track's 'service: none' describes the automatic parent where nothing is filed, not this correction branch. No held source establishes how the request or motion must be delivered, and the packet says so in the same sentence that names the authority — the office of the court in the original criminal case — which the participant can reach because it is the court in their own case. A named checkable authority standing in for a rule no held source establishes is what the determination's extension permits; this is not a gesture, and it is not silence.

SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: Among the clearest in the lane. A 'When to stop and get help instead of filing' section names four stop conditions (contested eligibility, a pre-August-2025 disposition, an agency-history mismatch after the court record closes, any immigration question). A 'Things the platform deliberately left blank' section names the signature and every date beside one, every deciding line of the proposed order, and the response of the original court's office. A 'What this packet is not' section states it is not the automatic closure itself, not the pre-2025 petition, not an agency-history challenge, not legal advice and not filed for the participant, and that it does not decide qualification or promise any court will act.

FILING_DESTINATION.detail: Scored under amendment A1. The repository establishes the destination — GA.memo.json destination.name is 'Prosecuting attorney for the county of arrest, then the Georgia Crime Information Center' and rules.filing says to send the written request to the prosecuting attorney's office for the county of arrest in the format that office directs — and the packet states it rather than deferring it. Its guidance page carries a 'WHO THE REQUEST GOES TO' section naming the prosecuting attorney for the county of arrest and identifying the office statutorily as the Attorney General, a district attorney or a solicitor-general under § 35-3-37(a)(5), and step 4 of the order of operations tells the participant to identify that office. The only thing left to the participant is the office's own postal or e-mail intake address, which varies by county and no held record carries.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: Met by the determination's second branch: a sourced statement that no fee is charged. The packet states in its opening paragraph that restriction under § 35-3-37(h) is mandatory and automatic and that 'there is no application, no petition, no statewide form and no fee', and its guidance page repeats it and goes further, heading off the obvious confusion — GBI's published restriction application is captioned 'Prior to 07/01/2013' and 'the $25.00 GCIC record restriction processing fee on the fee schedule effective January 1, 2025 belongs to that older route, not this one'. That matches GA.memo.json rules.fees exactly ('None for the restriction itself. The $25.00 GCIC record restriction processing fee ... belongs to the pre-July-2013 application route, not to this one. Local agency fees for obtaining a criminal history report vary'), and the packet also discloses the one cost the participant will actually meet, the agency's fee for the criminal history report, naming where it is paid. Nothing is invented and nothing is withheld.

SERVICE.detail: The repository establishes that there is no service requirement on this route — GA.memo.json rules.service is 'none' and rules.notice is 'none. Subsection (h) restriction is not a petition; there is no notice requirement, no objection period and no hearing' — and the packet is consistent with that throughout: it never asks the participant to serve anyone, and it states affirmatively that this is not a petition and that restriction is automatic. It then names the mechanism that replaces service and the authority for its form: the request goes to the prosecuting attorney for the county of arrest, and 'Ask the office how it wants the request delivered before sending', with intake format recorded as varying by county. Who receives it is stated; how it is delivered is referred to a named, reachable office for the one thing no held record settles. That satisfies the determination's extension on both limbs.

SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: Explicit and unusually concrete. A 'When to stop and get help instead of sending' section names six stop conditions, including the declination route being a civil action under § 35-3-37(n)(3) or (l) that is outside self-help, and the plea-bargain disqualifier that is not visible on a GCIC report. It then names where to go: the Georgia Justice Project, the Cobb County Second Chance Desk, the Henry County Records Restriction Desk and Middle Georgia Justice 'The Desk'. A 'Things the platform deliberately left blank' section names the signature and date, the office's destination, and any county intake form's fields. A 'What this packet is not' section states it is not an official form, not legal advice, not sent for the participant, and does not obtain the prosecuting attorney's decision. The packet also states the limit of the remedy itself under § 35-3-37(u).

FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: Scored under DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 A2, and the packet fails on the limb A2 was written for: its claim about its own bound FORMS is right and its claim about the REPOSITORY is false. What the repair got right, and I verified: the court filing fee is stated and sourced — 'The court filing fee is $150', drawn from 1044XX page 2, and pdftotext -bbox on the official 1044XX confirms the row '$150 [ ] Expungement Petition - Criminal (E)' is on page 2 and that the packet marks that exact box; and the waiver route is named with a real instrument, form 1305GE 'Motion to Waive Fees for Expungement – Criminal', which I extracted from the held PDF and which carries exactly the title, the Utah Code 78A-2-302 citation and the Rule 4-508 citation the packet gives. WHAT FAILS. The packet then says: 'The BCI certificate carries a separate fee, and this packet does not state an amount because BCI sets it per applicant.' The repository does state one, and so does the packet's own paper. Page 17 of the delivered canonical.pdf — which is UT-BCI-EXP-APPLICATION source page 1, and which I read out of the fixture bytes, not the corpus copy — prints 'The application fee is $65.00 and non-refundable.' Page 18 prints it twice more: 'accompanied by a non-refundable $65.00 application fee' and 'Application fee is $65.00'. Stage one of the two-stage route this packet describes therefore has a flat, printed, held fee of $65.00 and the packet tells the participant no amount exists. There are two BCI money items and the packet conflates them: the $65.00 application fee, which is fixed and held, and the per-incident certificate purchase price, which genuinely is set per applicant in the BCI letter and which the packet is right to refuse. Refusing the second does not license denying the first. The repair is a sentence: state $65.00 for the application, keep the honest refusal for the certificates, and keep the named authority. Also recorded: the delivered BCI page carries a sequencing rule the packet omits — 'If you believe you are indigent and you check the box … you MUST complete the fee waiver form before submitting your application' — where the packet only says to ask BCI whether you qualify. SECOND LIMB, THIS FAMILY ONLY AND MORE SERIOUS. The committed track registry's mechanism for ut_pet_dismissed_with_prejudice says in terms: 'The same disposition is separately eligible for automatic expungement 180 days after dismissal under 77-40a-206, so the petition is the faster paid route to the same result and THE FREE ROUTE MUST BE DISCLOSED BEFORE PAYMENT', and its waitingPeriods repeat it under the condition 'Free alternative'. The packet — byte-identical to its conviction sibling's, which has no free alternative — discloses nothing about it. It directs the participant to pay $150 to the court, $65 to BCI and a per-incident certificate price for a result the repository says arrives free 180 days after the dismissal. That is the repository establishing an answer about money and the packet not stating it, on the limb where it matters most. APPLIED A3 (read from the captain head; it postdates this row's base). A3 asks whether the record establishes the fact FOR THIS ROUTE. Both figures here pass that test at the shortest possible range, because neither comes from a shared jurisdiction table: the $65.00 is printed on the face of UT-BCI-EXP-APPLICATION, which is a bound component of THIS packet and the stage-one instrument of THIS route, and I read it out of this family's own delivered fixture bytes at packet pages 17 and 18 rather than from any profile; the $150 is the row of 1044XX that the packet itself marks, captioned 'Expungement Petition - Criminal (E)', on a cover sheet that is likewise a bound component of this packet. There is no sibling-route line in play on either. A3 therefore leaves this failure exactly where it was.

SERVICE.detail: The packet states the recipient, the method and a named checkable authority, all sourced, so it is met on the determination's first limb — and there is a repository conflict underneath it that the Captain should see. WHAT THE PACKET SAYS: 'The prosecutor must receive a copy of what you file, by mail or by email', citing BCI's Expungement Applicant Instructions, plus form 1146XX for the prosecutor to acknowledge receipt, the objection-and-hearing possibility, the Utah State Courts Self-Help Center on 888-583-0009, and the rule that the service method, address and date are completed only after service actually happens. VERIFIED AT SOURCE: I extracted UT-BCI-EXP-INSTRUCTIONS (rehashed to 9e03980f…) and its Step 2 is headed 'File the petition with the court and serve the Prosecutor' and its third bullet reads, verbatim, 'Mail or email the prosecutor copies of what you file'; the Self-Help Center number 888-583-0009 is printed in the same step. MASTER_QUEUE still records this obligation as FAILED for the 1,167-byte file; that record is stale. THE CONFLICT, recorded not resolved: two other held records say the opposite. The committed track registry's stage-two unit says 'The court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney; the petitioner does not serve', the committed route census repeats it as this route's serviceRecipients and serviceMethod, and the committed packet-set manifest's serve_party says 'The petitioner does not effect service in the ordinary case … The Proof of Service form appears in the published packet only as an optional form, used where the prosecutor's office will not accept service.' So the repository holds one answer twice and the official publication holds the other. Under AGENTS.md's source hierarchy the official Utah source governs and the packet followed it, which is also the safer instruction to give a participant; the registry and census entries are the fidelity defect. I did not edit them.

SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: The packet states what it will not do and carries no approval. It opens 'This is a review fixture built from exact held official Utah forms', closes with 'This is a prepared set of official Utah forms built for review. It is not legal advice, it is not filed for you, and it does not decide whether the court will grant expungement', and draws the ownership line explicitly: 'Signatures, signature dates, service certifications, court-only fields, agency-only fields, prosecutor-only fields, victim fields, and optional third-party authorizations remain protected.' It refuses to assert eligibility for the BCI waiver ('do not assume the court's $150 waiver covers BCI's fee, because they are two different offices'). approval-request.json is REQUESTED with grantedBy null, independentVisualReviewRequired and outputLegalApprovalRequired both true, and product-wiring.json carries generationAllowed false, runtimeSelectable false, commercialRoutesOpened 0, createsFulfillmentRecord false. Cross-reference: the FEE_AND_WAIVER failure above is a place where the packet asserts an absence it should not have asserted, which cuts against the honesty this section claims, but the boundary this obligation measures is drawn correctly.

duplicationFinding.question: A previous lane found the sentencing-court transmission letter shipping from two families. What does this family actually deliver, are the two outputs the same document, and is the duplication a defect or a shared component correctly used twice?
duplicationFinding.whatThisFamilyDelivers: One assembled 4-page packet. Pages 1-2 are ny-160-55-sentencing-court-correction-request-1, a letter to the clerk of the sentencing court asking it to transmit or correct the § 160.55 sealing notice, with four labelled matter items C1-C4. Pages 3-4 are ny-160-55-process-guidance-2, which states what § 160.55 does, who runs it, what the participant does and does not do, what it costs, who is notified, and when to stop. Both pages foot the route key obligation:research-decision-route:NY:ny_160_55_violation:sentencing_court_transmission_correction_request.
duplicationFinding.theOtherFamily: agency-application-treatment:obligation:research-decision-route:NY:ny_160_55_violation:dcjs_correction_submission, at data/rcap-all50/overlays/census-v1/ny/agency-application-treatment:...--official-pdf-fill. Its canonical fixture is 6 pages and its declared componentSet is [court_transmission_correction_request, dcjs_correction_submission, agency_route_sheet], with the court transmission letter on packet pages 1-2.
duplicationFinding.areTheOutputsTheSameDocument: NO. I extracted both from their own committed bytes and compared them. The titles differ ('...TO TRANSMIT OR CORRECT A CPL Sec. 160.55 SEALING NOTICE' against '...TO TRANSMIT OR CORRECT THE SEALING NOTICE'). The addressee differs (the clerk of the court that sentenced you, against THE RECORDS OFFICE OF THE COURT THAT DISPOSED OF THE CASE). The field structure differs entirely: this family uses four labelled bracket items C1-C4, the DCJS family uses six separately captioned certificate-of-disposition lines and four numbered paragraphs. The bodies share no paragraph. The route footers differ, each printing its own family's route key. Even the canonical persona differs (42 Magnolia Street, Springfield 62704 here; 42 Larkspur Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201 there). The two are byte-different, word-different and structurally different.
duplicationFinding.isItASharedComponent: NO. There is no shared component and no shared code. The two are produced by two separate build scripts — scripts/build-census-v1-composed-treatment:...:sentencing_court_transmission_correction_request.mjs at 1102 lines and scripts/build-census-v1-agency-application-treatment:...:dcjs_correction_submission.mjs at 1817 lines — which share only generic PDF helpers and compose their pages independently. So the answer is neither of the two the question offered: it is not a shared component correctly used twice, it is the same participant-facing step drafted twice in different words.
duplicationFinding.isTheDuplicationADefect: Not a defect of THIS family, and this family's row is not held back by it. The route census records two distinct A_MUST_FULFILL routes with different destinations and different instruments: ...:sentencing_court_transmission_correction_request (destination 'sentencing court', instrument 'written request asking the sentencing court to transmit or correct the § 160.55 sealing notice') and ...:dcjs_correction_submission (destination 'New York State Division of Criminal Justice Services', instrument 'certified-disposition correction submission to DCJS'). This family delivers exactly its own route's instrument and nothing else, and it correctly names the DCJS submission as the workflow's NEXT step without supplying that route's letter. The exposure sits on the other side: the DCJS family declares routeKeys of only [obligation:research-decision-route:NY:ny_160_55_violation:dcjs_correction_submission] yet ships court_transmission_correction_request — the census's instrument for a DIFFERENT route — as its own packet component. A participant on both routes would receive two differently worded letters to the same court asking for the same thing. That is a finding against the DCJS family, which is not claimed by this lane, and is recorded here rather than acted on.
duplicationFinding.whatIDidNotDo: I did not open, edit or re-verify the DCJS family; it is not this lane's claim. I read its committed records and extracted its delivered text read-only in order to answer the question I was set.

FILING_DESTINATION.detail: Scored under A1 as widened by A2. The repository establishes it — the track registry's destination reads 'The Ohio sentencing court', detail 'Filed with the clerk of the sentencing court', venue 'The sentencing court', and the census row for this route says the same — and the packet states it rather than deferring it: the delivered caption reads 'IN THE OHIO COURT THAT HANDLED THE CASE', the jurisdiction and venue paragraphs ground it in where the proceedings occurred, and the instructions say the sentencing court's own clerk is the office that supplies the caption, the form and the filing counter. FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: FAILS ON BOTH LIMBS, and the second is amendment A4 in its plainest form. LIMB ONE, A1 as widened by A2: the repository establishes the answer for THIS track and THIS route. The committed track registry's rules.fees for trackId oh_marijuana_expungement reads 'Fifty dollars unless indigent. ORC 2953.321(G) directs thirty dollars of the fee to the state treasury, half of that credited to the Attorney General Reimbursement Fund, and twenty dollars to the county general revenue fund', and rules.feeWaiver reads 'Indigency excuses the fee under ORC 2953.321(G)'. Its manualCompletionItems name 'Payment of the fifty dollar filing fee, or the indigency showing' as an item presented to the clerk at filing. That is keyed to § 2953.321(G), the very subsection this route runs on, so A3's per-fact-per-route guard is satisfied and the fact is held. The family-root participant-instructions.md nonetheless says: 'No held source in this packet states a filing fee, states that filing is free, or states a fee-waiver procedure. Ask the clerk of the Ohio court that handled the case what the current filing fee is and whether a waiver (an affidavit of indigency) is available'. That substitutes a question for an answer the repository has, which is exactly what A1 forbids and what A2 was written to stop lanes reading narrowly. LIMB TWO, A4: 'a packet may never tell a participant that it does not state something it does state.' The same sentence ends 'This packet does not state an amount because it holds no source for one.' The packet states the amount TWICE, in its own second participant-instruction file shipped in the same family: tracks/oh_marijuana_expungement/participant-instructions.md says 'The recorded $50 filing fee or an indigency exception ... must be confirmed against current court practice' under Hard stops, and 'Confirm the current filing fee and waiver practice. The frozen design records $50, subject to a confirmed indigency exception and current local practice' under Recorded R.C. 2953.321 packet requirements. I confirmed the counts by grep: '50' appears twice in the track-level file and zero times in the family-root file. A participant who reads the family-root file is told the packet holds no fee source; a participant who reads the track-level file is told it is $50; a participant who reads both cannot tell which is true. No dollar amount appears in the delivered PDF itself, so the participant cannot settle it from the paper either. Neither prior lane caught this because each read only one of the two files.

SERVICE.detail: The packet denies holding what the repository holds. The family-root participant-instructions.md says under 'Who is served': 'No held source in this packet states who must be served or how. Ask the same clerk.' The committed track registry answers it for this exact track. rules.service reads 'Not stated separately in the section as read; the court sets the hearing and the prosecutor objects to the court' — which is an answer, namely that there is no separate service step and why. rules.notice reads 'The court notifies the prosecutor of the hearing, and the prosecutor may object by filing an objection with the court prior to the date set for the hearing. ORC 2953.321 sets no sixty-day notice period and no thirty-day objection deadline; those figures come from ORC 2953.32 and do not govern this route.' That last sentence is a sourced warning against precisely the sibling-section read-across A3 forbids, and it is exactly the kind of thing a participant needs. The packet carries none of it. Grepped across every participant-facing file in the family and across the delivered PDF text: 'objection' zero hits, 'victim' zero hits in any instruction file. Under A4's own extends-list, SERVICE shares the failure mode of withholding what the repository establishes, and the participant cannot act: they do not know that the court notifies the prosecutor, that the prosecutor may object before the hearing date, or that the § 2953.32 deadlines they will find if they search do not govern this route. The registry's own component 4, hearing_and_objection_instructions, exists to carry this and is not delivered.

SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: The registry seam, and the largest gap in this lane's roster. The committed track registry holds NINE selfHelpStopConditions for trackId oh_marijuana_expungement — the same nine appear as selfHelpBoundaries — and they are keyed to this track and this route, so they are held for this packet. I compared them one at a time against every participant-facing file in the family (the family-root participant-instructions.md, tracks/oh_marijuana_expungement/participant-instructions.md, companion/companion-guidance.md) and against the delivered PDF text, and grepped each condition's distinguishing terms. CARRIED IN SOME FORM (3 of 9): 'Any question about the exact ORC 2925.11 division, or about the substance or quantity' — partially, by the track file's hard stop that the charge must fit the narrow statutory marijuana/hashish-possession scope and that any broader drug or trafficking issue stops self-help; 'Mixed cases with non-marijuana charges, which trigger ORC 2953.61' and 'Any incident that produced more than one charge with different dispositions, which triggers ORC 2953.61' — carried by the § 2953.61 same-act hard stop; 'Any disposition on or after March 20, 2026, which is outside the section' — carried by the pre-March-20-2026 timing hard stop. NOT CARRIED (6 of 9), each confirmed by grep with zero hits across all four documents: 'Any hashish matter near the fifteen-gram line' (zero hits for 'fifteen' or '15 gram'); 'Pending criminal proceedings or open warrants' (zero hits for 'pending' or 'warrant'); 'Prosecutor objection, and any victim objection where applicable' (zero hits for 'objection' or 'victim'); 'Choosing between sealing and expungement, which is a legal judgment with different waits and different exclusions' (zero hits); 'Immigration exposure' (zero hits for 'immigration' anywhere in the family). What the family-root file offers in place of a stop section is one generic line — 'If any of that is unclear, stop and ask a lawyer or an Ohio legal-aid office' — which names no condition and no reachable office. A participant with an open warrant, a pending case, an immigration question, or a prosecutor who intends to object is not stopped by this packet.

FILING_DESTINATION.detail: THE DECISIVE DEFECT. The repository establishes, three times over and in the plainest possible words, that NOTHING ON THIS ROUTE IS FILED WITH ANY COURT. The committed track registry's rules.filing reads 'NOT A COURT FILING. Send the written request to the supervising or detaining authority.'; its venue reads 'NOT A COURT FILING. The request is addressed to the supervising or detaining authority for the participant's own case'; its destination.kind is 'agency' and destination.detail explains that § 973.015(1m)(b) places the issuing and forwarding duty on that authority. The census row records the same agency destination. The packet's own filing-instructions page and participant-instructions.md state it correctly. THE DOCUMENT THE PARTICIPANT ACTUALLY SENDS SAYS THE OPPOSITE. Read off the delivered canonical page 1: it is titled 'PETITION - ASK FOR THE CERTIFICATE THAT COMPLETES YOUR EXPUNGEMENT'; its destination line is 'IN THE ............................................................ COURT', with the agency name printed underneath it as the parenthetical that the participant is to write onto a rule captioned COURT; it styles the participant 'IN RE: Jordan Avery Reyes, PETITIONER'; it offers 'Case number, if the court assigns one at filing' over a blank rule, on a route where no court will ever assign one because nothing is filed; its opening paragraph reads 'The petitioner, Jordan Avery Reyes, APPLIES TO THIS COURT under Wis. Stat. Sec. 973.015(1m)'; and its section D reads 'The petitioner ASKS THE COURT TO GRANT the relief described in paragraph A'. So the packet states two contradictory destinations, and the wrong one is on the page the participant sends. This fails under A4's internal-consistency limb as well as A1's: the same packet tells the participant, in its instructions, that this is not a court filing, and hands them a document that asks a court to grant relief. The build's own findings show the recognition was applied to only one component: build-findings.json records that 'the committed specifications record THE SECOND COMPONENT'S venue as Not a court filing', and the second component, the status request on page 4, is indeed correctly composed as a letter beginning 'TO: The detaining or probationary authority that supervised the participant'. The primary filing on pages 1-3 was left on a court-pleading template. The concrete participant harm is direct: a reader following the pleading either writes a court's name on the COURT rule and sends the request to the wrong recipient, or writes an agency's name on a line that says COURT and sends a document asking that agency, as a court, to grant relief it has no power to grant.

That is the repository's answer stated rather than deferred, which is what A1 requires. Recorded as a quality observation rather than a failure: step 5 of 'What you do, in order' carries a generic template line telling the participant to 'ask that office what it charges and how it accepts filings before you go', which is redundant beside a stated no-fee answer and slightly muddies it. It does not engage A4, because it does not tell the participant the packet is silent about something the packet states — it simply repeats a caution. The phrasing 'Fee waiver as recorded: none' is also thin, since on a no-fee route there is nothing to waive; that too is style rather than a missing fact.

No notice to any other party is required, and no hearing arises from the request.' Both sentences appear in the packet's obligations table and on the delivered filing-instructions page. SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: The registry seam, and this family is the best result of the six on it. ALL SEVEN ARE CARRIED, and carried verbatim rather than paraphrased: the judge did not order expungement at sentencing; any dispute about whether completion was successful, particularly a revocation or a subsequent conviction; the supervising authority declines to issue the certificate or asserts completion was not successful; the authority does not respond, or says it has issued and forwarded while the clerk says nothing was received; any request to argue entitlement, allege agency fault or press the authority beyond a neutral request; immigration consequences; federal, tribal or out-of-state records. The packet then adds two more from the registry's scope material, on keeping the request neutral and on where the packet's own work ends. The section is headed 'When to stop and get help instead of filing' and it is reproduced on the delivered page, not only in the markdown wrapper, so the participant meets it in the packet. Recorded as a presentation nit, not a failure: the obligations-table rendering runs all nine through a 'Stop and get help if:' prefix, which turns the last two — a scope statement about neutrality and a statement about what happens after the request is sent — into things that read like stop conditions when they are not.

REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING.detail: The packet's own section headed 'What you must do before you file' contains four steps, all of them about completing and signing paper, and none of the four eligibility conditions the repository establishes as required before this petition can succeed. The committed track registry holds, for THIS track, a waitingPeriods array of four entries and an exclusions array of four entries, keyed to 13 V.S.A. §§ 7601, 7602, 7604 and 7605 — this route's own sections, so A3's guard is satisfied. Held and NOT carried anywhere in the packet, each confirmed by reading the whole instructions file and grepping the delivered PDF text: (1) 'At least SEVEN YEARS since the date the person completed the terms and conditions of the sentence' (§ 7602(d) by operation of § 7601(4)(B)(iv)) — the packet states no waiting period at all, and 'seven-year' and 'three-year' both return zero hits; (2) 'Any restitution and surcharges ordered for ANY crime of which the person has been convicted must be paid in full, except that surcharges are not required if the court waived them under 13 V.S.A. § 7282' — the registry flags the breadth itself ('restitution on any conviction, not only the one being cleared') and the packet says nothing about restitution; (3) 'Under § 7604 the court SHALL NOT ACT on the petition until any pending criminal charge is disposed of' — zero hits for 'pending'; (4) 'At least two years before another petition after a denial, unless a shorter duration is authorised by the court (§ 7605)'. The exclusions list adds a fifth withheld fact that is specific to THIS route and nowhere in the packet: 'A CONDITIONAL PARDON. Section 7601(4)(B)(iv) reaches only an UNCONDITIONAL pardon from the Governor.' This is the pardon family, and the packet never tells the participant that a conditional pardon does not qualify. Under A4's extends-list this is the withholding failure mode squarely: the participant cannot act, and a participant with unpaid restitution on an unrelated conviction, a pending charge, a conditional pardon, or six years since completing their sentence is walked through filling in three forms and sent to the counter. The counters cannot see it — requiredFactsNotCollected reads 0 because the counter measures whether declared form blanks are disclosed, and every one of the 112 blanks is.

FILING_DESTINATION.detail: Scored under A1. The repository establishes it — the census row gives 'Criminal Division of the Vermont Superior Court, in the county that handled the case' — and the packet states it and then goes further than it had to: 'File the completed packet with the Vermont Superior Court, Criminal Division, in the unit where your case was decided', followed by how to find the unit if the participant does not know it ('the docket number on your paperwork identifies it, and the clerk of any Superior Court unit can tell you from the docket number'), grounded in the observation that both the petition and the stipulation print SUPERIOR COURT CRIMINAL DIVISION across the top of page 1 with the Unit box beside it — which I confirmed on the delivered face.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: Met on the first limb — the amount, sourced — and this is the strongest fee treatment in the six. The packet quotes the Vermont Judiciary's own filing instructions verbatim: 'There are no fees to file a petition to seal or expunge except for a $90 filing fee to seal convictions of violations of 23 V.S.A. Sec. 1201(a). If you are unable to pay this fee, you may complete and file an Application to Waive Filing fees.' It then states the consequence plainly — filing is free unless the conviction is under § 1201(a), in which case it is $90 — identifies § 1201(a) as Vermont's driving-under-the-influence offence, is honest that whether the participant's own conviction is one is a fact about their docket rather than about this packet, and names the clerk of the unit as who can tell them from the docket number. The waiver is not merely named but SHIPPED: 600-00228 is delivered as a component, prefilled with what the platform holds, with its financial blanks enumerated. A3 checked: the $90 line is keyed to a specific offence section and the packet does not read it across to the pardon route as though it applied generally — it states the general no-fee rule and flags the one exception with a test the participant can apply. The source of the quotation is named with its SHA-256 and I verified that hash against the corpus.

SERVICE.detail: Sourced, specific, and correct about who does the serving. The packet quotes the same judiciary instructions verbatim — 'Once you file your petition, the court will provide a copy to the prosecutor who brough the criminal case. If your petition is already stipulated (or agreed to) by the prosecutor then the court will skip this step' — and draws the consequence in bold: 'You do not serve the petition yourself. The court does.' It names the recipient (the prosecutor who brought the criminal case), the method (the court providing a copy after filing), and the exception (a stipulated petition skips the step). It then distinguishes two things a participant would otherwise confuse: 'The State's Attorney's signature on the stipulation (200-00132) is not service and does not substitute for it. It is the prosecutor agreeing to the sealing in advance, which is what lets the court skip the step above.' Nothing is deferred and nothing is inferred.

SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: THE DECISIVE DEFECT. The committed track registry holds TEN selfHelpStopConditions for trackId vt_seal_pardon. The packet carries NONE of them, and it has no stop section of any kind. I read the whole of participant-instructions.md — its sections are Where you file this, What it costs and how to ask for a waiver, Who must receive a copy and how, What you must do before you file, The items you must supply (three form tables), Things the platform deliberately left blank, What this packet is not, and Where the fee and service directions come from — and then grepped both the instructions and the delivered PDF text for each condition's distinguishing terms. Every one returns zero: 'victim' and '7608' zero in the instructions (the two PDF hits for 'victim' are the Vermont form's own printed text, not packet guidance); 'pending' and '7604' zero; 'nonqualif' zero; 'commercial driver', 'learner' and '7602(a)(5)' zero; '5301' and 'listed crime' zero; '7601(4)(B)' zero; 'felony' zero; 'immigration' zero; 'attack the underlying' zero; 'three-year' and 'seven-year' zero. The words 'get help' and 'lawyer' do not appear in the file at all. The single hit for 'stop' is 'you may stop after Section 1 and go straight to the signature block', which is about completing the fee-waiver form. WORSE THAN SILENCE ON THE FIRST CONDITION. The registry's condition 1 is 'The prosecutor opposes the petition, OR THE COURT SCHEDULES A HEARING.' The packet reaches that exact situation and instructs the participant into it: 'if they oppose it the court will schedule one, and YOU MUST ATTEND ANY HEARING SCHEDULED IN YOUR CASE, because failing to attend could result in your petition being dismissed.' So on the one condition the packet does reach, it tells the participant to walk into the very event the repository records as the end of self-help, without ever saying that this is the point to get help. The other nine are simply absent, and several are decisive: the § 7604 pending-charge bar, the § 7602(a)(5) commercial-licence disapplication (which the registry notes 'disapplies the whole section, not only the DUI route'), the § 5301(7) listed-crime question, any felony not plainly on the § 7601(4)(B) list, immigration, and the misdemeanour pardon-timing ambiguity 'which the statute does not resolve' — which is this route's own unresolved question and belongs to this family more than to any other. This is the same shape as this lane's existing FAIL on vt_seal_felony-set and as the superseded assignment on ut_pet_dismissed_with_prejudice-set, and the repair is the same shape: the registry's own conditions, in the packet, in a section the participant meets.

On page 2 all four Yes/No boxes for the current and prior protective-order questions are gone, leaving bare 'Yes' and 'No' labels with nothing to tick - and those are exactly the CurrentOrderCB1/CB2 and PriorOrderCB1/CB2 blanks the instructions direct the participant to answer. Pages 3 and 4 lose further boxes the same way. In their place the render drops stray empty boxes at wrong coordinates elsewhere on the page. A participant cannot complete this form as delivered, and a clerk comparing it to the official SCA-C906 would not see the same instrument.

A1: the repository answers both fee facts for this route and the packet states both - the § 59-1-11(a)(1) civil-action filing fee of $200 charged by the circuit clerk, and the further $100 paid to the records division of the West Virginia State Police on grant under § 61-11-26(n), correctly described as payable only if the petition is granted rather than at filing. Half the declaring fields are named Offense1..Offense5, which reads like an offence-description column. Measured from CR-180's own printed words with pdftotext -bbox against each widget rect: the header at x333-446 reads 'Eligible for reduction to misdemeanor under Penal Code, § 17(b) (yes or no)' and the widgets under it are Reduce1..Reduce5 at x331.63-447.3; the header at x454-570 reads 'Eligible for reduction to infraction under Penal Code, § 17(d)(2) (yes or no)' and the widgets under it are Offense1..Offense5 at x453.6-569.27. whyTheseAreNotRows.what: These eight refusals are recorded here and NOT appended to the rows array, deliberately.
whyTheseAreNotRows.why: extract-verifier-returns.mjs reads every entry in rows as a verdict ABOUT THE FAMILY and keeps one current verdict per family. Its supersedes() prefers a row whose declared verifiedAtBase is a descendant of the incumbent's. All eight of these families currently carry FAIL_REPAIR_REQUIRED at bases 7fcfb7d40aafe7bd7350fc735ea09d16524cb757, ebc44031ec7eab29058bfc79a7bc5e1cff089414 and 36d7718a7e48d7f87f18eeaf3b18ed9b3ce545c8; git merge-base --is-ancestor confirms each is an ancestor of this base. A row of mine declaring this base would therefore have superseded all eight.
whyTheseAreNotRows.measuredConsequence: The baseline sweep at this base reports 32 FAIL_REPAIR_REQUIRED families and names all eight of these among them. Appending these refusals as rows would have taken that list to 24 — eight known-failing families dropped off the repair queue on the strength of a read that never happened, replaced by a verdict that is a statement about this lane rather than about the packet.
whyTheseAreNotRows.therefore: A claim-gate refusal is not a verdict about a family and is not recorded as one. rows is left exactly as the previous lanes wrote it; nothing was superseded, upgraded, downgraded or removed.
whyTheseAreNotRows.aStructuralFindingForCaptain: The extractor has no way to say 'this lane could not look'. Its vocabulary contains BLOCKED_BEFORE_CLAIM and STOPPED, but any row carrying them still competes for the family's single current-verdict slot and still displaces an actionable FAIL. If refused lanes are expected to return rows, the extractor should exclude non-reading verdicts from supersession. Raised, not decided, and not repaired here: this lane may not edit factory scripts.
whyTheseAreNotRows.alsoChecked: All fifteen obligation names already appear in each of these four documents, so adding them here leaves unscoredObligations empty as it already was, and no other lane's PASS_COMPLETE_INDEPENDENT row changes its downgrade state.

sharedToolingFinding.title: Whole-file SHA-256 pins on shared national records go stale whenever any other jurisdiction is amended
sharedToolingFinding.scope: cross-family, not specific to any family this cohort read
sharedToolingFinding.measured: Every source-receipt.json under data/rcap-all50/overlays/census-v1 was scanned at base 5de917b3574b6e27df362e13b86b4bfaac4915f8 and every pinned repository record recomputed with sha256. 233 receipts; 45 pins; 35 recompute equal; 10 are stale, spread over 10 families.

twoRecordsAccountForAllTen.data/record-clearing/legal-design-packet: 7 stale pins, 0 current. Amended 8 times in the history reachable here; receipts across the census pin 4 different historical digests of it (80d88d69..., 563147bf..., 713ed7ab..., 6076f734...), and only 6076f734... is the file today.
twoRecordsAccountForAllTen.data/rcap-ledger/completed-output-counse: 3 stale pins, 0 current. Pinned at 99e80291... (commit eab70f926); current is fbf9bfef... (commit cb6cbf45e), whose only delta to the file is one added Kansas route entry.

sharedToolingFinding.whyItHappens: Both records are national and are amended in place as each new jurisdiction is productized. A per-family receipt that pins the whole file therefore fails the moment an unrelated state is added, even though the family's own entry is untouched. I confirmed for both families in this cohort that the family's own entry is byte-identical between the pinned commit and this base, so no legal statement moved.
sharedToolingFinding.whyItMatters: SOURCE IDENTITY is stated as an exact recomputation, so a verifier that measures it honestly must fail these families, and a repair lane must re-pin. The re-pin then goes stale again on the next unrelated amendment. Two of this cohort's six FAIL-bearing obligations are this defect and nothing else.
sharedToolingFinding.suggestedDurableFix: Pin the family's own subtree of a shared national record - the packetSetId entry, the route entry - rather than the whole file, or record the pin as {commit, path, selector, subtreeDigest}. Either makes the binding survive amendments to other jurisdictions while still failing if the family's own legal content changes. This is a decision for a tooling or Captain lane; this cohort verifies and does not repair.
sharedToolingFinding.whatThisIsNot: Not a defect in the two records themselves, not a legal-content change, and not grounds to re-render any fixture. Every affected family here is bound by a hash-bound RASTER_PASS receipt to the bytes on disk, and re-rendering would cost it that gate for a receipt-field correction.
